audit.whatIsWrong: Early text says neither side has an engage tool at level 3 and treats the lane as a pure poke war.
audit.why: Gravity Field (W) is online at 2 and stuns anyone who stays in it; Charm is online at 3. From level 2 this is a commit war, not just poke. Ahri's Q is 970 range vs Hextech Ray's 525, which is the real early lever.
audit.corrected: Poke from Q range on his last-hit step; never stand in Gravity Field; from 3 both sides hold a commit tool.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes referenced fabricated ability names and gave no cooldown anchors.
audit.why: Viktor's spikes are augment-driven (Glorious Evolution Hex Fragments) plus Gravity Field 17/16/15/14/13s; Ahri's are 6, Malignance, Shadowflame.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten to Siphon Power / Gravity Field / Hextech Ray / Arcane Storm with real cooldowns; augment denial added to the ahead line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabricated names — 'Power Transfer' (really Siphon Power, Q), 'Death Ray' (really Hextech Ray, E), 'Chaos Storm' (really Arcane Storm, R). The decisive interaction was never stated.
audit.why: Arcane Storm carries the channel flag ('interruptible — any CC cancels it') and Charm (E) is hard CC at 975 range, so Charm cancels his 120/100/80s ultimate outright. Siphon Power is a shield plus auto-reset, so a 'won' trade can come back even.
audit.corrected: Charm cancels Arcane Storm mid-channel; trade after he spends Siphon Power on a minion (9/8/7/6/5s); leave Gravity Field before the stun ticks.

audit.why: Spell-shield/QSS/tenacity behaviour is not in the kit text and was not asserted.

edits.before: Viktor's Power Transfer poke and shield trade evenly with your Orb of Deception harass — whoever lands Death Ray or Charm cleanly through minions wins the exchange, so this stretch comes down to skill.
edits.after: Viktor's Siphon Power poke and shield trade evenly with your Orb of Deception harass — but Hextech Ray is 525 range to your 970, so poke from max range and make him step in to answer you.

edits.before: Chaos Storm is a delayed-damage ultimate with no hard CC, so your Spirit Rush lets you burst and reposition faster than he can punish, giving you the cleaner all-in window.
edits.after: Arcane Storm is a channel — Charm cancels it outright, and Spirit Rush puts you in charm range the moment he casts, so his 120-second ultimate can vanish on impact.

edits.before: Right after his augment upgrade (usually Gravity Field or Death Ray augment) he starts to zone you off farm hard with AoE denial, but your burst is still faster if you catch him out of position.
edits.after: After his first augment (usually Gravity Field or Hextech Ray) he zones you off farm with AoE denial, but Gravity Field is down 13-17 seconds — step up on that timer and your burst still lands first.

edits.before: Fully scaled Viktor with all augments and a completed Death Ray/Storm combo out-damages you in extended fights and safely zones entire areas, making him the stronger late-game mage.
edits.after: Fully augmented Viktor out-damages you in extended fights and zones whole areas with Hextech Ray and Gravity Field, so refuse the long fight and take him with a flank charm instead.

edits.before: Early trades are close and mechanical — both of you are poking with a skillshot/orb and neither has a hard engage yet, so whoever lands Death Ray or Charm cleaner through minions gets the edge. Viktor's shield from Power Transfer makes some trades feel neutral even when you land your poke, so don't overcommit chasing small pokes. This phase is genuinely even and comes down to who plays it tighter.
edits.after: Early trades are close and mechanical — your Q outranges Hextech Ray 970 to 525, so poke on his last-hit step and walk before he answers. Siphon Power shields him and resets his auto, so a trade you won can come back even; step in on its 9-second cooldown. From level 2 Gravity Field stuns anyone who lingers in it — cross the zone, never fight inside it. The lane is even and rewards the tighter player.

edits.before: At 6 you pull ahead: Chaos Storm has a windup and no direct CC, so if you engage with Charm first he has almost no way to stop your combo before you're already resetting with Spirit Rush. Look to punish him hard here, especially right after he uses Power Transfer on a minion since his shield is down. This is your best all-in window in the whole matchup.
edits.after: At 6 you pull ahead: Arcane Storm is a channel, so Charm cancels it outright and a 120-second ultimate is gone the moment he commits. Punish right after he spends Siphon Power on a minion — no shield, and its 9-second cooldown is your window. Spirit Rush's three dashes make the charm angle he cannot ward, so this is your best all-in of the lane.

edits.before: Once Viktor gets his augment upgrades (typically boosted Death Ray or Gravity Field) and a completed mythic-tier build, his zone control and raw damage output start to exceed yours in extended fights — he can safely poke and area-deny without ever needing to commit. Your job late is to force short trades and pick him off before a fight drags out, because a straight sustained fight favors him once he's scaled.
edits.after: Once Viktor's augments land (typically Hextech Ray or Gravity Field) and his items complete, his zone control and damage exceed yours in extended fights — he pokes and area-denies without ever committing. Your job is to end fights before they start: flank with Spirit Rush, charm him off the Gravity Field he set, and burst him down. If Arcane Storm goes up, Charm interrupts the channel and the fight resets in your favour.

edits.before: Still an even skill-based exchange with no reliable engage tool yet on either side.
edits.after: Charm and Gravity Field are both online now — this is a commit war, not a poke war.

edits.before: Your ultimate gives a cleaner, faster all-in than his delayed-damage ult, a real advantage for you here.
edits.after: Spirit Rush gives a faster all-in, and Charm cancels the Arcane Storm channel outright — a real edge here.

edits.before: Look for all-in windows right after he uses Power Transfer
edits.after: Look for all-in windows right after he uses Siphon Power

edits.before: Farm safely behind Power Transfer shield procs
edits.after: Farm safely behind Siphon Power shield procs

edits.before: Land Death Ray/Gravity Field augment combos to zone the wave
edits.after: Land Hextech Ray/Gravity Field augment combos to zone the wave

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Viktor wins by stunning you in Gravity Field into Hextech Ray, then farming augments while you never find an angle.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget R Spirit Rush (last dash) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — 17s at rank 1, 13s maxed. Leave the zone before the stun ticks, then step up on that downtime. - Siphon Power is his shield and auto-reset on a 9s cooldown; trade after he spends it on a minion.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry through picks — charm Viktor out of his Gravity Field or cancel Arcane Storm mid-channel, and his fight becomes yours.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt the map: shove with Q, dash-flank every river, and charm-pick Viktor's teammates until the lane lead is a game lead.
edits.after: Ahead, deny augments: shove with Q so he misses waves, then dash-flank other lanes — every Hex Fragment he never earns is a spike deleted.

edits.before: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Q out and back through where he last-hits so both hits land — the return is true damage and Siphon Power's shield still eats it.

edits.before: Q through his last-hit so both hits land, W if he eats the return, and walk — repeat until the charm window is lethal instead of optimistic.
edits.after: Charm his step-up or his Arcane Storm channel — the ultimate dies on cast and a 120-second cooldown buys you the whole mid-game.

edits.before: Viktor spends Gravity Field early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Passive heals at 9 minions — clear with Q, bank the heal, then trade at full health.

edits.before: That is Viktor’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: The last dash is your exit from Gravity Field — keep one.

edits.before: The last dash is your life insurance — an Ahri who spends all three going in is an assassin's favorite story.
edits.after: A missed charm is 12 seconds with no answer to his step-up — hold it for his commit, not for chip damage.

edits.before: Charming on cooldown for chip damage and then facing his real engage with nothing — the charm is the matchup, not the poke.
edits.after: With Gravity Field up he can stun you mid-trade and chain Hextech Ray — check that 13-17s cooldown before you step into range.

edits.before: Track Viktor’s Gravity Field: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Gravity Field (17s at rank 1): the stun tick owns every all-in. And Charm cancels Arcane Storm — his channel dies the second you land it.
